s1.syndrome_frame: Painless facial mass with deep tissue involvement and no systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Firm, mobile, non-tender mass in the left buccal space
Well-defined, firm, non-tender mass on intraoral palpation
key_facts: 25-year-old woman presented with a painless lump in the left cheek
Lump was first noted nine months earlier
No toothache, numbness, or systemic symptoms
No significant medical history
Left facial asymmetry without skin changes on examination
Mass was approximately 4 cm in diameter and located deep in the left buccal space
No cervical lymphadenopathy was noted
Intraorally, there was a bulge of the left buccal mucosa
Ultrasonography showed a discrete, well-demarcated, hypoechoic solid mass
Contrast-enhanced CT revealed a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy yielded a hypocellular sample with no signs of malignancy
Intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrated wide fibroblast proliferation

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common benign salivary gland tumor, consistent with painless lump and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Wide fibroblast proliferation on biopsy, consistent with fibromatosis

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the location and characteristics of the mass, although less likely than pleomorphic adenoma

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the location and characteristics of the mass, although less likely than pleomorphic adenoma

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the location and characteristics of the mass, although less likely than pleomorphic adenoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor with a hypocellular sample showing no signs of malignancy and an intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrating wide fibroblast proliferation is most consistent with a pleomorphic adenoma, which is a common benign salivary gland tumor.

rejected.label: Fibromatosis
rejected.why: Fibromatosis is a more aggressive condition that typically presents with infiltrative growth and a higher rate of recurrence, which is not consistent with the well-bordered nature of the tumor in this case.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipoma is a benign tumor composed of fat tissue, which is not supported by the ultrasonography or CT findings in this case.

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibroma is a benign nerve sheath tumor that typically presents with a more heterogeneous appearance on imaging and may be associated with neurofibromatosis type 1, which is not suggested in this case.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannoma is a benign nerve sheath tumor that typically presents with a more heterogeneous appearance on imaging and may be associated with neurological symptoms, which are not present in this case.
